# Input
Input is a set of controls that lets you play Neon Pairs with a pointer, touch or keyboard.

Status: spec version 2.2.

You can reveal a card with a tap, then move to its partner with the arrow keys. Every activation uses the same game action, so changing input methods keeps the same turn.

## Activation

The card controls follow these rules:

- I01 - Render each card as a native button. A primary click, a completed tap, Enter and Space activate the card through the same action.
- I03 - Keep the browser's normal context menu on right-click or long-press. Opening that menu doesn't activate a card.
- I04 - Hover and pointer cancellation leave the game state unchanged.

The game decides whether an activation changes a card. See [Rules](rules.md) for matches, repeated selections, blocked turns and turn timing.

## Keyboard movement

- I05 - Give the board one remembered tab stop. When Tab enters the board, focus that card. Use the first card before any board focus has been remembered.

- I06 - Move focus with these keys. Movement changes focus without activating a card:

| Key | Focus destination |
| --- | --- |
| ArrowLeft | Previous card in the same row |
| ArrowRight | Next card in the same row |
| ArrowUp | Card in the previous row and same column |
| ArrowDown | Card in the next row and same column |

The board handles only these four arrow keys without modifiers, plus Enter and Space. It leaves every other key and modifier combination to the browser and doesn't use them to move focus or activate a card.

- I07 - Stop arrow movement at a board edge. Moving left from the first column keeps focus on the same card.

- I08 - Let native Tab and Shift+Tab leave the board. Moving through the board uses the movement keys instead of adding every card to the page's tab order.

## Focus

The board keeps focus separate from play:

- I09 - Keep matched cards focusable and mark them `aria-disabled="true"`. Their game action follows the matched-card rule in the gameplay document.
- I10 - While a mismatching pair waits to turn back, allow focus movement and block card activation.
- I11 - On initial load, keep the browser's current focus. Loading the game doesn't move focus to the board.
- I12 - After a new deal, Restart or a successful load, reset the board's remembered tab stop to its first card.
- I13 - When a card receives focus, scroll it into view with nearest alignment in the board's scroll area. Give each card a scroll margin of at least 6px, so its complete focus outline stays in view, including mid-board cards.

The session buttons keep their focus as defined in [Controls](controls.md).

## Card names

The button names describe the information available to the player:

- I14 - Name a hidden card by its one-based row, column and closed state. Keep its face SVG and face identifier out of the DOM while it is hidden, including attributes and accessible text.
- I15 - Name a revealed or matched card by its position, face name and state. Use the face names defined in [Visuals](visuals.md).

For example, the first hidden button is named "Row 1, column 1, closed". Once revealed, its name includes the face, so a player can remember it without seeing the drawing.

## Announcements

- I16 - Use one polite, atomic live region for turn results and completion. Announce each turn result exactly once. A winning turn has one announcement containing both the match and the win. Consecutive identical results each get their own announcement. Focus movement, clock renders and closing a mismatch don't repeat a result.

Use these turn announcements, where `M` is the matched pair count, `N` is moves and `time` uses R07's display format:

| Event | Announcement |
| --- | --- |
| First match | Pair found. 1 pair matched. |
| Later match | Pair found. M pairs matched. |
| Miss | No match. Cards close after a short pause. |
| Final match | Pair found. All pairs found in N moves and time. |

Send the load statuses in Controls through this same live region once per load event. Keep the visible status beside the reproduction controls.

For example, moving across three cards leaves the current announcement unchanged. Resolving the next pair announces that turn's result.

## Screen reader

- I17 - Support a complete 4x4 keyboard game with a screen reader. Find Grid size and New Game by name, enter the board, expose closed positions and revealed faces by name and state, announce one result per turn and make the win, final moves and time available. Leave the board with Tab and start another game. Deliver automated accessibility-tree evidence for this journey. Record the browser and tool versions in the project README and say whether a screen reader was used. If one was used, record its name and version. The user confirms spoken output during acceptance. Spoken confirmation isn't the developer's deliverable.

The complete game pack starts in [Neon Pairs](README.md).

# Acceptance
Acceptance is a set of journeys that checks whether Neon Pairs meets its product requirements.

Status: spec version 2.2.

Finish a game, then start another one during a mismatch. The first journey checks play and completion. The second checks that an earlier timer can't change a new game.

## Play

Use these journeys with the requirements in [Rules](rules.md):

- Finish every supported size with complete pairs.
- Reveal one card twice, then reveal a different card. Check the exact move count.
- Match a pair, then miss a pair. Check the immediate match and the 800ms active mismatch interval.
- Hide the page during a mismatch, then return and finish its remaining interval.
- Start and restart during a mismatch. Check the cleared state and later timer updates.
- Finish games with better, equal and worse move counts. Reload and check the current size's best.

## Controls

Use pointer, touch and keyboard to follow [Input](input.md) and [Controls](controls.md). Check control labels, row movement, edge stops, native Tab exit and focus after each action. Check that hidden cards reveal no identity in the DOM.

Follow the keyboard journey in I17 and check its accessibility tree. During user acceptance, confirm spoken results with a screen reader, including consecutive identical results and the final match with its win.

## Appearance

Measure the layout and review all 128 faces against [Visuals](visuals.md). Use a 44px grayscale face sheet to distinguish shape, marker and fill. Check 16x16 boards at both stated viewport sizes, full focus outlines and the equivalent zoom layout. Check reduced motion and the static completion banner after its single pulse.

Play through completion and reset while checking [Sound](sound.md). Every action stays silent.

## Reproduction

Check [Reproducibility](reproducibility.md) with its example deck and replay. Check snapshot round trips and malformed input. Check the exact mismatch timeout before an equal-time replay action.

Load an unfinished snapshot, attempt input while paused, then Resume. Check its remaining active time and focus. Load a completed snapshot and check its static banner and unchanged best score.

## Delivery

Use a locked install, type check, unit tests and a fresh browser build as defined in [Technology](technology.md). Open the resulting HTML directly from disk with network access blocked. Use a local HTTP origin for saved preferences.

Review the pure game functions, browser effects, file sizes and behavior placement against [Architecture](architecture.md).

Back to [Neon Pairs](README.md).

name: sites
description: Use Sites when the user wants a website built for them (including a landing page, portfolio, dashboard, portal, tracker, hub, game, event registration, or tool), requests changes to a website already built with Sites, wants to publish a website with Sites, or wants to manage Sites hosting.

# Sites

Take the requested website through the supported development and publishing workflow. Publish completed new Sites and edits unless the user requests local-only work or saving without deployment. New Sites start private; preserve an existing Site's audience unless the user requests a change. Native tool approvals apply without an additional conversational publishing gate.

For hosting-only changes, use the relevant native Sites tool and confirm its returned state; source preparation is needed only for source changes or publication.

## Workflow

`<plugin-root>` is the installed directory containing `scripts/` and `skills/`. Run helpers with absolute paths and literal arguments from the selected checkout. Keep credentials in session memory and pass them through stdin, never shell arguments, files, or output.

### 1. Select and open

Default to a new Site unless a specific existing Site is identified.

- **Existing hosted Site:** retain its `project_id` and audience, call `get_site` and `create_source_repository_write_credential`, and open with the [source helper](#source-helper) before editing. Omit `archivePath`; use an empty directory when source is missing, then the returned `checkout_path`.
- **New Site:** create a unique, new empty project subdirectory in the task's workspace, normally `/workspace/sites/<slug>` in managed Linux. Default simple pages and browser-local interactions to buildless HTML/JS; use the supplied Vinext starter for server behavior. Preserve retained templates.
- **Local-only:** use the available checkout; skip registration, source synchronization, and publication.

### 2. Prepare and launch

For new Vinext projects, run:

```text
node <plugin-root>/scripts/project-setup.mjs
```

This copies the starter and configures ignored checkout-local state. Helpers select `managed-linux` only for `SITES_MANAGED_LINUX_CONTAINER=1`, otherwise `portable`. For buildless HTML/JS, prepare `dist/` for `index.html` and assets; skip starter setup, installation, and build.

For a retained template, add `--template-source <absolute-sanitized-source-directory>`; exclude Site identity, Git metadata, credentials, and runtime data. For explicitly requested Worker ESM, add `--starter worker-esm` and follow [its README](templates/worker-esm-starter/README.md). Use [Troubleshooting](references/troubleshooting.md#project-configuration) for profile repair or static-to-Worker migration.

After minimal setup, launch registration for new hosted work in a retained execution cell when available. Native `create_site` creates a private, unpublished Site and returns its ID and source credential. Immediately persist the ID when it returns. For static Sites, include `--static-directory` when known to set both fields at once; omit it for Worker builds. For buildless HTML/JS, run:

```text
node <plugin-root>/scripts/set-project-id.mjs --project-id <returned-id> --static-directory dist
```

Reuse an existing ID or registration attempt; resolve uncertain creation before retrying. For app integrations, first read [discovery and declarations](references/app-integrations.md#discover-and-declare).

Start needed dependency installation before feature implementation:

```text
node <plugin-root>/scripts/install-dependencies.mjs
```

Run only when dependencies are missing or their inputs changed. The installer handles host settings, package-manager selection, and interrupted setup; it takes no flags. Use one installer; keep dependency inputs unchanged while it runs. Proceed to implementation once the applicable operations are launched.

For managed-image pnpm additions, use `node "$SITES_PNPM_BIN" add <package>`.

Start required image search or generation when its brief is clear, alongside independent source work. Consider a parallel subagent for image downloads. Delegate bounded asset or research tasks; the Site owner handles the checkout, native Sites calls in the owning conversation, and publication.

### 3. Implement

Write application files while setup runs. For hosted work, await persisted Site identity before further manifest edits or source synchronization. Await installed dependencies before commands that need them.

Implement the requested experience in one focused pass; revise for observed failures or unmet requirements. Replace starter title and description and remove temporary `codex-preview` metadata during implementation. Integrate required assets and complete the requested behavior before publishing.

# Architecture
Architecture is the code structure for Neon Pairs that keeps game rules separate from browser effects.

Status: spec version 2.2.

A card activation changes game data first. React renders that data, then the session adapter handles time and saved preferences. The same rules run in browser tests and replay without a browser.

## Game core

- A01 - Keep deck generation, card transitions, logical time, snapshot validation and replay as pure functions under `src/game`. They receive their inputs directly. They don't read the DOM, storage, external random sources or browser clocks.

- A02 - Keep the board description and deck immutable. Keep matched positions, current selection, moves, active elapsed milliseconds and whether play started in game state. Derive pair count and victory. Serialize progress using the [reproducibility formats](reproducibility.md).

- A03 - Use direct calls and exhaustive branches for the closed, one-card and mismatch states. Keep named states, format versions, timing values and size limits beside the behavior they control.

Proposed game functions:

| Call | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `createGame(boardCode)` | Initial state for a valid board code |
| `activateCard(state, index)` | State after one card activation |
| `advanceGame(state, milliseconds)` | State after logical time advances |
| `isWon(state)` | Whether every position is matched |
| `encodeSnapshot(state)` | Version 1 snapshot JSON |
| `decodeSnapshot(text)` | Valid restored state or `null` |
| `replayGame(text)` | Final replay state or `null` |

## Browser session

- A04 - Keep React state, timer lifecycle and browser visibility handling in `src/game/session`. Use a monotonic browser clock. Clear pending work on unmount and invalidate callbacks when the deal changes. A callback from an earlier deal can't change the current one.

- A05 - Keep preference and best-score reads in the session storage module. Treat saved JSON as unknown input. Validate grid sizes and finite integer scores. Catch read, parse and write failures. Keep unrelated storage keys untouched. A failure leaves the game playable.

- A06 - Keep active game progress in memory until you export or import a snapshot. Importing a completed snapshot doesn't update best scores or play a celebration. Completing an unfinished imported game records a local best under R10.

## Components

- A07 - `Game.tsx` composes status, the board, game controls and reproduction controls. Keep board navigation in `src/game/board`, controls in `src/game/controls` and session behavior in `src/game/session`. Keep each component's props and styles beside it.

- A08 - A card mounts its face SVG only while revealed or matched. Hidden card identity stays out of DOM attributes, accessible names and diagnostic globals. Tests can know a deck from its documented board code. The app gives them no solver endpoint.

- A09 - Use native browser input and the shared card activation function. Keep focus position in the board component. Focus movement changes presentation, never the deck or move count. [Input](input.md) defines the keys and focus rules.

## Evidence

- A10 - Keep focused tests beside their behavior. Complete browser journeys live at the application test level. Check generation against independent literal vectors. Check game transitions against stated rules. Test built HTML from disk as well as served storage behavior.

- A11 - Keep development fixtures and diagnostic helpers out of the shipped game. Tests can use the documented board code, snapshot and replay formats. The shipped game exposes only its documented controls.

## Changes

- A12 - Add a new rule at its game behavior, then update its component, tests and specification. Add shared support only when two actual behaviors need the same meaning. Don't add a global store, event bus, router or generic utility folder.

The [game specification](README.md) defines the behavior this structure implements.

# Controls
Controls is a specification that defines the game options and reproduction tools in Neon Pairs.

Status: spec version 2.2.

You can start another deal, repeat the current one or load saved progress. Each control keeps the same label, so you can find the same action after a game changes.

## Deal controls

The main controls are:

- C01 - Label the native size select "Grid size". Give it options `4x4`, `6x6`, `8x8`, `10x10`, `12x12`, `14x14` and `16x16`, with numeric side length `N` as each value. After a successful board-code or snapshot load, select the loaded board's size.
- C02 - Label the fresh-deal button "New Game". It creates a fresh seed and keeps the current size.
- C03 - Label the repeat-deal button "Restart". It starts the same board code again.

Changing size, starting and restarting follow the session rules in [Rules](rules.md).

## Reproduction tools

- C04 - Put reproduction controls inside a native `details` element that starts collapsed. Give its summary the exact text "Reproduce a game".

The controls use the board-code and snapshot formats defined in [Reproducibility](reproducibility.md). A board code starts a deal. A snapshot loads progress on a deal.

## Load a board

- C05 - Label the text input "Board code" and limit it to 32 characters. Show the current board code after a new deal, Restart or a successful load. Keep an edited draft when a card action changes the game.

- C06 - Label its button "Load board". Validate the entered code before replacing the current game with that deal's starting state.

For example, loading `np1-4-1` starts its hidden four-column board. Entering that code alone keeps the current game until you select Load board.

## Snapshot tools

- C07 - Label the textarea "Snapshot JSON" and limit it to 65536 characters. The parser also applies the UTF-8 byte limit in the snapshot format.

- C08 - Label the export button "Export snapshot". Fill the textarea with readable version 1 snapshot JSON that you can select and copy manually. Export leaves the game state and clock unchanged. It requires no Clipboard API.

Export `elapsedMs` and a pending mismatch's `remainingMs` as whole milliseconds. A pending mismatch always exports at least 1ms.

- C09 - Label the import button "Load snapshot". Validate the complete draft before replacing the current game. Load unfinished progress paused and show "Loaded snapshot. Select Resume to continue." Load completed progress as completed without pausing and show "Loaded completed snapshot."

- C10 - Show a "Resume" button only while an imported unfinished game is paused. Selecting it clears that pause. Unfinished play continues from the loaded state. While paused, block every card activation and allow board focus movement. On Resume, move focus to the board's remembered tab stop before removing the Resume button. A loaded completed game stays completed and shows no Resume button.

- C11 - On invalid input, keep the current game and the entered draft for correction. Show the exact status for that control:

| Control | Status |
| --- | --- |
| Load board | Invalid board code. |
| Load snapshot | Invalid snapshot. |

- C12 - A loaded completed snapshot keeps the win banner static and plays no celebration. Import doesn't write a best score. Resuming an unfinished snapshot and later winning records a local best under R10.

For example, loading a completed game with fewer moves than the saved best shows that game without replacing the saved record.

## Focus

- C13 - Keep focus on the button used for starting, restarting, loading or exporting. These actions don't move focus to the board. Resume follows C10 because its button disappears. The board's remembered tab stop follows the focus rules in [Input](input.md#focus).

## Replay

- C14 - Keep replay in the developer CLI and game core. V1 has no replay controls in the game UI.

Run `npm run --silent replay -- PATH` to read a replay file. On valid input, print only the final snapshot JSON to stdout and exit 0. On invalid input, print nothing to stdout, write a message to stderr and exit nonzero.

The complete game pack starts in [Neon Pairs](README.md).

# Input
Input is a set of controls that lets you play Neon Pairs with a pointer, touch or keyboard.

Status: spec version 2.2.

You can reveal a card with a tap, then move to its partner with the arrow keys. Every activation uses the same game action, so changing input methods keeps the same turn.

## Activation

The card controls follow these rules:

- I01 - Render each card as a native button. A primary click, a completed tap, Enter and Space activate the card through the same action.
- I03 - Keep the browser's normal context menu on right-click or long-press. Opening that menu doesn't activate a card.
- I04 - Hover and pointer cancellation leave the game state unchanged.

The game decides whether an activation changes a card. See [Rules](rules.md) for matches, repeated selections, blocked turns and turn timing.

## Keyboard movement

- I05 - Give the board one remembered tab stop. When Tab enters the board, focus that card. Use the first card before any board focus has been remembered.

- I06 - Move focus with these keys. Movement changes focus without activating a card:

| Key | Focus destination |
| --- | --- |
| ArrowLeft | Previous card in the same row |
| ArrowRight | Next card in the same row |
| ArrowUp | Card in the previous row and same column |
| ArrowDown | Card in the next row and same column |

The board handles only these four arrow keys without modifiers, plus Enter and Space. It leaves every other key and modifier combination to the browser and doesn't use them to move focus or activate a card.

- I07 - Stop arrow movement at a board edge. Moving left from the first column keeps focus on the same card.

- I08 - Let native Tab and Shift+Tab leave the board. Moving through the board uses the movement keys instead of adding every card to the page's tab order.

## Focus

The board keeps focus separate from play:

- I09 - Keep matched cards focusable and mark them `aria-disabled="true"`. Their game action follows the matched-card rule in the gameplay document.
- I10 - While a mismatching pair waits to turn back, allow focus movement and block card activation.
- I11 - On initial load, keep the browser's current focus. Loading the game doesn't move focus to the board.
- I12 - After a new deal, Restart or a successful load, reset the board's remembered tab stop to its first card.
- I13 - When a card receives focus, scroll it into view with nearest alignment in the board's scroll area. Give each card a scroll margin of at least 6px, so its complete focus outline stays in view, including mid-board cards.

The session buttons keep their focus as defined in [Controls](controls.md).

## Card names

The button names describe the information available to the player:

- I14 - Name a hidden card by its one-based row, column and closed state. Keep its face SVG and face identifier out of the DOM while it is hidden, including attributes and accessible text.
- I15 - Name a revealed or matched card by its position, face name and state. Use the face names defined in [Visuals](visuals.md).

For example, the first hidden button is named "Row 1, column 1, closed". Once revealed, its name includes the face, so a player can remember it without seeing the drawing.

## Announcements

- I16 - Use one polite, atomic live region for turn results and completion. Announce each turn result exactly once. A winning turn has one announcement containing both the match and the win. Consecutive identical results each get their own announcement. Focus movement, clock renders and closing a mismatch don't repeat a result.

Use these turn announcements, where `M` is the matched pair count, `N` is moves and `time` uses R07's display format:

| Event | Announcement |
| --- | --- |
| First match | Pair found. 1 pair matched. |
| Later match | Pair found. M pairs matched. |
| Miss | No match. Cards close after a short pause. |
| Final match | Pair found. All pairs found in N moves and time. |

Send the load statuses in Controls through this same live region once per load event. Keep the visible status beside the reproduction controls.

For example, moving across three cards leaves the current announcement unchanged. Resolving the next pair announces that turn's result.

## Screen reader

- I17 - Support a complete 4x4 keyboard game with a screen reader. Find Grid size and New Game by name, enter the board, expose closed positions and revealed faces by name and state, announce one result per turn and make the win, final moves and time available. Leave the board with Tab and start another game. Deliver automated accessibility-tree evidence for this journey. Record the browser and tool versions in the project README and say whether a screen reader was used. If one was used, record its name and version. The user confirms spoken output during acceptance. Spoken confirmation isn't the developer's deliverable.

The complete game pack starts in [Neon Pairs](README.md).

# Acceptance
Acceptance is a set of journeys that checks whether Neon Pairs meets its product requirements.

Status: spec version 2.2.

Finish a game, then start another one during a mismatch. The first journey checks play and completion. The second checks that an earlier timer can't change a new game.

## Play

Use these journeys with the requirements in [Rules](rules.md):

- Finish every supported size with complete pairs.
- Reveal one card twice, then reveal a different card. Check the exact move count.
- Match a pair, then miss a pair. Check the immediate match and the 800ms active mismatch interval.
- Hide the page during a mismatch, then return and finish its remaining interval.
- Start and restart during a mismatch. Check the cleared state and later timer updates.
- Finish games with better, equal and worse move counts. Reload and check the current size's best.

## Controls

Use pointer, touch and keyboard to follow [Input](input.md) and [Controls](controls.md). Check control labels, row movement, edge stops, native Tab exit and focus after each action. Check that hidden cards reveal no identity in the DOM.

Follow the keyboard journey in I17 and check its accessibility tree. During user acceptance, confirm spoken results with a screen reader, including consecutive identical results and the final match with its win.

## Appearance

Measure the layout and review all 128 faces against [Visuals](visuals.md). Use a 44px grayscale face sheet to distinguish shape, marker and fill. Check 16x16 boards at both stated viewport sizes, full focus outlines and the equivalent zoom layout. Check reduced motion and the static completion banner after its single pulse.

Play through completion and reset while checking [Sound](sound.md). Every action stays silent.

## Reproduction

Check [Reproducibility](reproducibility.md) with its example deck and replay. Check snapshot round trips and malformed input. Check the exact mismatch timeout before an equal-time replay action.

Load an unfinished snapshot, attempt input while paused, then Resume. Check its remaining active time and focus. Load a completed snapshot and check its static banner and unchanged best score.

## Delivery

Use a locked install, type check, unit tests and a fresh browser build as defined in [Technology](technology.md). Open the resulting HTML directly from disk with network access blocked. Use a local HTTP origin for saved preferences.

Review the pure game functions, browser effects, file sizes and behavior placement against [Architecture](architecture.md).

Back to [Neon Pairs](README.md).

# Neon Pairs
Neon Pairs is a browser memory game that asks you to find every pair of matching cards.

Status: spec version 2.2.

Reveal two cards at a time and finish in as few moves as you can. A board code repeats a deal, so you can report a problem with the same starting cards.

Choose a size, then reveal a card and find its partner. Matches stay face up. A miss closes both cards after 800 active milliseconds. Finding every pair completes the game with your moves and time. The game draws faces on a dark background. Shape, marker and fill distinguish each face without color. Layout, colors, motion, 16x16 behavior and zoom are in [Visuals](visuals.md). The game stays silent as defined in [Sound](sound.md).

## Repeat a game

A board code describes a deal. A snapshot saves progress. A replay records timed actions. The algorithms and version 1 formats are in [Reproducibility](reproducibility.md). Spec version 2.2 doesn't change those format versions.

## Build

Use React, TypeScript and native DOM controls. Package pins, commands and the offline HTML distribution are in [Technology](technology.md). Pure game functions, browser effects and behavior placement are in [Architecture](architecture.md).

Use the journeys in [Acceptance](acceptance.md) to check the finished game. Those examples add no rules beyond the requirement IDs in their defining documents.

The game doesn't need to support these, so they're never tested:

- Keys and modifier combinations beyond the ones in [Input](input.md#keyboard-movement), which stay with the browser
- Holding a key down
- Several tabs or windows of the game open at once, where each tab may simply overwrite the saved preferences

  chooseSize = (size: Size): void => {
    if (size === this.view.game.board.size) return;
    this.replace(requireGame(boardCode(size, this.environment.seed(this.view.game.board.seed))), false);
  };

  private invalid(status: string): false {
    this.view = { ...this.view, status };
    this.announce(status);
    this.emit();
    return false;
  }

  loadBoard = (text: string): boolean => {
    const game = createGame(text.trim());
    if (!game) return this.invalid('Invalid board code.');
    this.replace(game, false, 'Loaded board.');
    return true;
  };

  loadSnapshot = (text: string): boolean => {
    const game = decodeSnapshot(text);
    if (!game) return this.invalid('Invalid snapshot.');
    const complete = isWon(game);
    this.replace(game, !complete, complete ? 'Loaded completed snapshot.' : 'Loaded snapshot. Select Resume to continue.');
    return true;
  };

  exportSnapshot = (): string => {
    this.settle();
    this.emit();
    return encodeSnapshot(this.view.game);
  };

  resume = (): void => {
    if (!this.view.paused) return;
    this.settle();
    this.view = { ...this.view, paused: false };
    this.emit();
  };

# Sites

Take the requested website through the supported development and publishing workflow. Publish completed new Sites and edits unless the user requests local-only work or saving without deployment. New Sites start private; preserve an existing Site's audience unless the user requests a change. Native tool approvals apply without an additional conversational publishing gate.

For hosting-only changes, use the relevant native Sites tool and confirm its returned state; source preparation is needed only for source changes or publication.

## Workflow

`<plugin-root>` is the installed directory containing `scripts/` and `skills/`. Run helpers with absolute paths and literal arguments from the selected checkout. Keep credentials in session memory and pass them through stdin, never shell arguments, files, or output.

### 1. Select and open

Default to a new Site unless a specific existing Site is identified.

- **Existing hosted Site:** retain its `project_id` and audience, call `get_site` and `create_source_repository_write_credential`, and open with the [source helper](#source-helper) before editing. Omit `archivePath`; use an empty directory when source is missing, then the returned `checkout_path`.
- **New Site:** create a unique, new empty project subdirectory in the task's workspace, normally `/workspace/sites/<slug>` in managed Linux. Default simple pages and browser-local interactions to buildless HTML/JS; use the supplied Vinext starter for server behavior. Preserve retained templates.
- **Local-only:** use the available checkout; skip registration, source synchronization, and publication.

### 2. Prepare and launch

For new Vinext projects, run:

```text
node <plugin-root>/scripts/project-setup.mjs
```

This copies the starter and configures ignored checkout-local state. Helpers select `managed-linux` only for `SITES_MANAGED_LINUX_CONTAINER=1`, otherwise `portable`. For buildless HTML/JS, prepare `dist/` for `index.html` and assets; skip starter setup, installation, and build.

For a retained template, add `--template-source <absolute-sanitized-source-directory>`; exclude Site identity, Git metadata, credentials, and runtime data. For explicitly requested Worker ESM, add `--starter worker-esm` and follow [its README](templates/worker-esm-starter/README.md). Use [Troubleshooting](references/troubleshooting.md#project-configuration) for profile repair or static-to-Worker migration.

After minimal setup, launch registration for new hosted work in a retained execution cell when available. Native `create_site` creates a private, unpublished Site and returns its ID and source credential. Immediately persist the ID when it returns. For static Sites, include `--static-directory` when known to set both fields at once; omit it for Worker builds. For buildless HTML/JS, run:

```text
node <plugin-root>/scripts/set-project-id.mjs --project-id <returned-id> --static-directory dist
```

Reuse an existing ID or registration attempt; resolve uncertain creation before retrying. For app integrations, first read [discovery and declarations](references/app-integrations.md#discover-and-declare).

Start needed dependency installation before feature implementation:

```text
node <plugin-root>/scripts/install-dependencies.mjs
```

Run only when dependencies are missing or their inputs changed. The installer handles host settings, package-manager selection, and interrupted setup; it takes no flags. Use one installer; keep dependency inputs unchanged while it runs. Proceed to implementation once the applicable operations are launched.

For managed-image pnpm additions, use `node "$SITES_PNPM_BIN" add <package>`.

Start required image search or generation when its brief is clear, alongside independent source work. Consider a parallel subagent for image downloads. Delegate bounded asset or research tasks; the Site owner handles the checkout, native Sites calls in the owning conversation, and publication.

### 3. Implement

Write application files while setup runs. For hosted work, await persisted Site identity before further manifest edits or source synchronization. Await installed dependencies before commands that need them.

Implement the requested experience in one focused pass; revise for observed failures or unmet requirements. Replace starter title and description and remove temporary `codex-preview` metadata during implementation. Integrate required assets and complete the requested behavior before publishing.

When `SITES_MANAGED_LINUX_CONTAINER=1`, preview is internal QA. Start it only when the task needs browser QA and `cua_repl.js` is available. If `cua_repl.js` is unavailable, skip browser QA: do not start a preview server, install a browser, or improvise another browser-control path.

When `SITES_MANAGED_LINUX_CONTAINER` is not `1`, use local preview. In visible tasks with user-facing preview support, show the first recognizable version once it serves successfully and keep it current. Background tasks skip user-facing handoff.

Before any preview, browser test, or screenshot, read the selected reference: [managed](references/preview/managed.md) or [local](references/preview/local.md). If preview infrastructure is unavailable, report the verification limit and continue appropriate checks and publication unless passing browser QA is required. Follow [Troubleshooting](references/troubleshooting.md#preview) after failures.

### 4. Validate and package

Collect any remaining registration and installation results, then finalize the source manifest before checks/builds and packaging.

#### Hosting manifest

The tracked `.openai/hosting.json` declares Site identity and deployment configuration. After registration, a minimal static Site uses:

```json
{
  "project_id": "<returned-id>",
  "static": {"directory": "dist"}
}
```

| Field | Contract |
| --- | --- |
| `project_id` | Persist with `set-project-id.mjs` on creation; preserve on updates. |
| `static` | Object with `directory`: `dist`, `dist/client`, `out`, `build`, or `.output/public`. Omit for Worker builds. |
| `d1`, `r2` | [Storage bindings](references/storage.md#bindings); leave unused bindings `null`. |
| `capabilities` | Declare [a Site MCP server](references/site-mcp-server.md#build-the-server) when needed. |
| `plugins`, `connectors` | [App integration declarations](references/app-integrations.md#discover-and-declare). |

Preserve existing fields. Edit the source manifest; build helpers emit Worker deployment metadata.

Run checks appropriate to the change; lint only when requested. For hosted work, package with the source helper using remaining checks/builds as ordered argument arrays and an absolute `archivePath`. Pass the complete prior opening result as `source` when available.

Buildless HTML/JS uses `commands: []` when no checks remain. Framework projects, including Vinext and static exports, build with `["node", "<plugin-root>/scripts/build-site.mjs"]`. Omit commands already completed successfully with unchanged inputs. Local-only work runs checks/builds directly and skips packaging for publication.

#### Source helper

Use the repository access from registration or `create_source_repository_write_credential` for the same Site. If `auth_mode` is `work_proxy`, it contains no token. Use the same helper or ordinary Git with `remote_url`; Work supplies authentication outside the executor. If Git reports expired access, call `create_source_repository_write_credential` again. Do not configure a token or authentication header for this mode.

```text
node <plugin-root>/scripts/site-workflow.mjs --project-id <project_id>
```

Launch with `exec_command(tty: true, yield_time_ms: 1000)`. After `Ready for Site workflow JSON on stdin (input is hidden).`, send one newline-terminated JSON object with `write_stdin`. Wait for successful exit and retain the final JSON result.

| Input | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `credential` | Returned credential object, through stdin only. |
| `source` | Complete prior opening result, when available. |
| `commands` | Remaining checks/builds as ordered argument arrays; packaging only. |
| `archivePath` | Absolute output archive path for packaging; omit for opening. |

The helper owns Git preparation, ordered commands, commit/push, and packaging. Pass its verified `project_id`, `commit_sha`, and `archive` directly to publishing; keep the archive unchanged until saving succeeds.

### 5. Publish

Use the audience from creation or `get_site`; refresh unknown or changed ownership/access before selecting a tool.

| Audience | Native calls |

| Other supported audiences | `save_site_version` then `deploy_site_version`. |

Save-only uses `save_site_version` without deployment. A matching archive-backed saved version needs only deployment; source-only versions still need their matching archive. Preserve returned version IDs, including `saved_version_id`, when resuming. Continue an existing deployment rather than starting another.

### 6. Finish

Poll `get_deployment_status` only for `pending`, `building`, or `publishing`; stop on a terminal result. A successful native result with its URL verifies deployment without another status call or browser visit.

Return the literal deployed URL, saved version for save-only work, or local result. In visible tasks, open the deployed URL in the existing Site tab with `open_in_codex` or equivalent when supported; background tasks skip browser handoff. Handoff failure does not invalidate a verified deployment. Report incomplete verification or blockers; read [Troubleshooting](references/troubleshooting.md) after a failure or incomplete result.

## Design

Build around the user's primary task. Choose a coherent visual direction suited to the subject and audience, and preserve established branding when editing. Keep layouts responsive, text readable, and interactions accessible. Use imagery when it contributes to the experience.

Keep functionality within the requested scope. For open-ended presentation-led briefs, develop content and structure as needed for a complete experience. Preserve explicit content constraints and keep bounded edits bounded.

Read applicable guidance before choosing content and structure. Select by the experience's purpose, not merely its visual subject.

*** Update File: /work/README.md
@@
 # Neon Pairs
-Neon Pairs is a browser memory game that asks you to find every matching pair.
+Find every matching pair on boards from 4x4 to 16x16. Play with a mouse, touch, or keyboard. The game is silent.
 
-Read [Neon Pairs game specification and document map](docs/README.md) to build the game.
+Open **[dist/index.html](dist/index.html)** directly in a browser. Its JavaScript, CSS, and SVG artwork are inline; play needs no server or network. Use a local HTTP origin when checking saved size preferences and best scores, because browser storage behavior on `file:` URLs varies. If storage is blocked, play and records remain available for the current session.
 
-Follow the requirements in docs/ for this project.
+The [product specification](docs/README.md) defines the game; [Architecture](docs/architecture.md) defines its structure.
+
+## Develop and build
+
+Use Node.js 24.19 or later and npm. Dependencies are pinned in `package.json` and `package-lock.json`.
+
+| Command | Result |
+| --- | --- |
+| `npm ci` | Install exactly the locked packages |
+| `npm run dev` | Start the local development server |
+| `npm run typecheck` | Check the separate browser and Node compiler projects |
+| `npm test` | Run colocated unit and replay-command tests |
+| `npm run build` | Type check, then emit the standalone `dist/index.html` |
+| `npm run test:e2e` | Build current source, then test that build in fresh Chromium contexts |
+| `npm run --silent replay -- examples/replay.json` | Print the replay's final snapshot JSON |
+
+For browser tests on a new machine, install the browser with `npx playwright install chromium`; Linux may also require `npx playwright install-deps chromium`. Browser tests manage their own HTTP server and stop it afterward. A failed build stops `test:e2e` before any earlier distribution can be tested.
+
+## Repeat or save a game
+
+Open **Reproduce a game**, enter `np1-4-1` in **Board code**, and choose **Load board** to reproduce the published example deal. **Restart** repeats the current code; **New Game** creates another deal.
+
+**Export snapshot** fills **Snapshot JSON** with readable JSON for manual copying. Paste saved JSON and choose **Load snapshot** to restore it. Unfinished imports pause both the clock and a pending mismatch until **Resume**. Completed imports show a static summary and do not change best scores. Progress is not automatically saved across reloads.
+
+Replay is a CLI feature. Its [example file](examples/replay.json) matches the first published pair and ends at 800 active milliseconds. Valid files print only the final version 1 snapshot to stdout and exit 0. Invalid or unreadable files print an error to stderr, leave stdout empty, and exit nonzero. See [Reproducibility](docs/reproducibility.md) for the exact board-code, snapshot, and replay formats and limits.
+
+## Code placement
+
+- `src/game`: pure deal generation, turns, logical time, snapshot validation, and replay.
+- `src/game/session`: the local React session, monotonic browser clock, visibility, preferences, and best scores.
+- `src/game/board`: native card buttons, SVG faces, roving keyboard focus, and scrolling.
+- `src/game/controls`: native deal and reproduction controls.
+- `src/game/Game.tsx`: composition, statistics, completion banner, and one result live region.
+- Colocated `*.test.ts`: focused behavior tests; `tests/`: complete built-application journeys and evidence generation.
+
+No development fixture, solver endpoint, diagnostic global, external asset, audio API, or service is included in the distribution. Authored TypeScript files are at most 200 lines.
+
+## Verified compatibility and acceptance
+
+Verified on 4 November 2026 with **Node 26.12.1, npm 11.20.0, Playwright 1.64.1, and Chromium 156.0.8078.4**. This is the compatibility combination named by the specification. All package versions match its pins.
+
+| Check | Result |
+| --- | --- |
+| `npm ci` | Passed; locked install, 50 packages, no reported vulnerabilities |
+| `npm run typecheck` | Passed; all authored source, unit tests, browser tests, and tooling checked |
+| `npm test` | Passed; 137 tests in 10 files, including literal generation vectors and actual replay-command output/exit checks |
+| `npm run build` | Passed; one 240,221-byte `dist/index.html` |
+| `npm run test:e2e` | Passed; 27 browser journeys against a fresh production build |
+| `npm run --silent replay -- examples/replay.json` | Passed; final snapshot has one pair, one move, and 800 elapsed milliseconds |
+
+Browser checks finish every supported board size; cover ignored turns, exact mismatch boundaries, replacement timers, snapshot validation and pauses, best-score comparisons/reload, unavailable storage, keyboard focus, accessible names, repeated live announcements, native touch swipes, and direct-from-disk play with networking blocked. Hidden-page handling is checked with injected visibility events in the browser and injected monotonic time in session tests; it is not a claim of native tab-background testing.
+
+The [keyboard accessibility-tree evidence](evidence/accessibility.md) records the complete 4x4 journey, revealed names, matched states, one result per turn, final summary, native Tab exit, and starting another game. **No screen reader was used.** Spoken output and a real-device long press remain user acceptance, as specified in [Input](docs/input.md) and the [specification scope](docs/README.md).
+
+The [44px grayscale sheet](evidence/faces-grayscale-44px.png) contains all 128 face identities, reviewed for shape, marker, and fill distinctions including diagonal squares. Layout, internal scrolling, and complete focus outlines were measured at 360x800, 1280x800, and 640x400 with device scale 2 for the last viewport, covering 4x4 and 16x16 boards. Screenshots: [phone](evidence/layout-360.png), [desktop](evidence/layout-1280.png), [equivalent 200% zoom](evidence/layout-640.png).
*** Add File: /work/examples/replay.json
+{"version":1,"boardCode":"np1-4-1","actions":[{"atMs":0,"index":0},{"atMs":0,"index":11}],"endMs":800}
*** End Patch"));
